plain.li: Mended my boots by lamplight and thought about the long table at home.
[summer] Long light evenings out here. I sit outside and count the days until the relief comes.
[outpost:Mining] Found a good seam today. The others will want to hear about it when I'm back.
[outpost:Mining] Rock dust in my food, my bed and my ears. The ore pile's bigger, though.
[outpost:Logging] The stack of cut timber is taller than me now. I measured, out of boredom.
[outpost:Logging] Sharpened the axes after supper. The woods are very quiet after dark.
[outpost:Farming] Weeded the long rows until my back gave out. They look tidier than the fields at home.
[outpost:Farming] Rain came at the right time for once. I stood in it and watched the furrows fill.
[outpost:Hunting] Spent the morning in a blind, waiting. The afternoon was worth it.
[outpost:Hunting] Hung the meat to dry and kept the foxes off it half the night.
[outpost:Defensive] Walked the palisade at dusk and again before dawn. Nothing moved but the wind.
[outpost:Defensive] Scouts went past in the distance. They saw us and kept going, which is what we're here for.
[outpost:Trading] A trader tried to sell me the same knife twice in one day. I bought it the second time.
[outpost:Trading] Counted the stores and the silver twice. Both came out right, which is a good day here.
[outpost:Science] Filled another notebook. Half of it is questions I can't answer yet.
[outpost:Science] Took the same readings morning and evening for a week. Something is changing, slowly.
[outpost:Town] Market day in town. I came back with less money and more news.
[outpost:Town] Someone in town asked where I'm from. I told them about home and didn't stop for a while.
[outpost:Scavenging] Pulled a whole crate out of the rubble today, unbroken. Most days it's just rust.
[outpost:Scavenging] Cut my hand on old metal. Washed it well. The haul was worth the scratch.
[outpost:Encampment] Travelers at the fire again tonight. One of them sang, badly, for hours.
[outpost:Encampment] Mended a stranger's cart wheel for a meal and a story. Fair trade.
[outpost:Fishing] Pulled in nets all morning. My hands smell of fish no matter how I scrub them.
[outpost:Drilling] The drill ran all day. I hear it in my sleep now.
[outpost:Factory] Long shift at the benches. Everything I made today will be home before I am.
[outpost:Production] Kept the work going from dawn to dark. The crates for home are stacking up.
[outpost:Artillery] Cleaned and checked the guns again. We haven't fired them in days. I hope it stays that way.

warm.li: The others out here are good company. Still, I miss everyone at home.
I've been saving the best stories from out here for when I get home.

blunt.li: Still here. Still working. Send news.

cheerful.li: Saw a herd crossing the plain at sunrise today! I wish everyone at home could have seen it.
The outpost's doing well, and so am I! I've even learned to like the cooking.

gloomy.li: Another week out here. I wonder if they've forgotten my face at home.
The outpost is quiet. Too quiet to stop me thinking.

cold.li: The outpost meets its quota. I'll stay until it doesn't.
Out here, nobody wastes my time. I find I prefer it.

plain.li: Tea at the end of a long day. I drank it standing at the window.
Someone left the pot warm. I had the last cup and refilled it for the next person.
[night] A cup of tea when I couldn't sleep. It didn't help me sleep, but it helped.

warm.li: Brought a cup of tea to whoever was on watch. We drank it together and didn't say much.
Tea with friends after supper. The best hour of the day.

blunt.li: Tea. Hot. That's all I ask.

cheerful.li: Tried the new tea! It's either very good or very strange, and I'm having another cup to decide.
A cup of tea and a sit-down! Small pleasures are the best pleasures.

gloomy.li: Tea went cold while I was thinking. Drank it anyway.
A cup of tea. For a few minutes, nothing else mattered.

cold.li: A cup of tea before the evening's work. It helps me concentrate.
Good tea is a sign of a well-run storeroom. Ours is adequate.

plain.li: Picked my way out past the stockpile in the rain to find somewhere to go. We need a latrine.

warm.li: Showed the newest one where people go when there's nowhere to go. I apologized while I did it.

blunt.li: Dug a hole. Used it. Filled it. Someone build a latrine.

cheerful.li: Out in the bushes at dawn I saw a deer, and it saw me, and we both pretended we hadn't.

gloomy.li: Every trip behind the woodpile is a reminder of how far we haven't come.

cold.li: Waste outside the walls is a disease waiting to happen. I've marked a place for a latrine.

plain.li: Bad day. Washed my clothes out at the creek before anyone was up.

warm.li: Someone found me a change of clothes and didn't say a word about why. I owe them.

cheerful.li: Not my finest hour. I've decided it never happened, and tomorrow I'll believe it.

gloomy.li: I'll be hearing about today in my head for a long while.

cold.li: An accident. The cause was distance to a toilet, and distance can be fixed.

plain.li: Waited outside the latrine so long I forgot what I'd come out for, and then remembered all at once.

warm.li: Two of us waiting by the latrine, both pretending we weren't. We ended up laughing.

cheerful.li: I've learned to time my trips around everyone else's. It's practically an art.

gloomy.li: Spent half the afternoon hopping from foot to foot. Dignity is a luxury here.

cold.li: One latrine for this many people is a planning failure. I've raised it.

plain.li: Boiled my water tonight after what happened yesterday. It still tasted of mud.

warm.li: I strained the water through a cloth for the others before they drank. It's the least I could do.

blunt.li: Water tastes like the ditch. Somebody fix it.

cheerful.li: The water was brown, but I'm choosing to call it tea.

gloomy.li: Even the water here is trying to kill us.

cold.li: The water source is contaminated. Find another, or expect sickness.

plain.li: A long hot soak after a long day. I fell asleep in the tub and woke up cold.
Hot water and a scrub brush. I'm a different person.

warm.li: A hot bath, then I warmed more water for whoever came next. It's how I'd want to be treated.

cheerful.li: The bath was so hot I turned pink, and I loved every minute!

gloomy.li: A hot bath. The ache came back as soon as I got out, but it was gone for a while.

cold.li: A hot bath. The time it takes is repaid by a clear head.

plain.li: Someone walked in on me at the latrine. We've agreed to never mention it, which is why I'm writing it here.

warm.li: Walked in on someone washing, by accident. I said sorry three times and left a towel by the door.

cheerful.li: Someone barged in on my bath, so I offered them a scrub. They left very quickly!

gloomy.li: No privacy, not even for washing. I'm too tired to be embarrassed anymore.

cold.li: Interrupted again. A latch costs less than the time I've lost to this.

plain.li: [good] Washed my hair properly today, after a week of not. It's a different color.
[bad] Working in the dirt all week, and no time to wash it off.

warm.li: [good] Washed and changed before supper, so I'd be decent company for once.
[bad] I'm filthy, but I'll wash once the others have had their turn.

blunt.li: [bad] Dirty. Busy. Too busy to care.

cheerful.li: [good] Clean hands, clean face, clean shirt! I feel like a new person.
[bad] I'm so dirty I could grow turnips on my neck!

gloomy.li: [good] Clean for a day. Tomorrow I'll be back in the muck.
[bad] Dirt in every crease. I've stopped noticing, which worries me.

cold.li: [good] Washed. Clean people are taken more seriously.
[bad] I'm unwashed and it shows. That needs fixing before the next trader comes.

plain.li: [good] A cold rinse after the fields. Felt like jumping in a river.
[bad] Cold water, cold room, cold feet. I washed what I had to and nothing more.

warm.li: [good] Cold water and good company at the wash basin. We laughed at each other's yelps.
[bad] Cold wash again. I'll ask whether we can spare fuel to heat the water for the old ones, at least.

cheerful.li: [good] Cold splash in the morning. I yelled so loud the chickens scattered!
[bad] The water was freezing, so I washed very, very quickly. Record time!

gloomy.li: [good] The cold water woke me up, which is more than I wanted.
[bad] A cold wash on a cold day. My teeth are still chattering.

cold.li: [good] Cold water. Bracing, and no fuel wasted.
[bad] Cold wash. A heater for the water would pay for itself in morale.

plain.li: [good] Took my time washing this morning, with nobody knocking. A small luxury.
[bad] The drain in my bathroom backs up. I've been bailing it with a cup.

warm.li: [good] I let a friend use my bathroom while theirs is being fixed. It's nice to have something to share.
[bad] My bathroom's grim, but at least it's mine. I'll fix it up bit by bit.

blunt.li: [good] My bathroom. My time. Nobody waiting.

cheerful.li: [good] I have my own bathroom, and I've hung a little mirror in it!
[bad] My bathroom's tiny. I bang my elbows every time, but it's all mine!

gloomy.li: [good] A bathroom of my own. I keep waiting for someone to take it away.
[bad] My bathroom is dark and damp, like the rest of my life.

cold.li: [good] A private bathroom. It saves me a quarter of an hour every morning.
[bad] My bathroom is poorly built. I've noted the faults.
